claim_1.claim: ELISA analysis of serum from 30 healthy young adults vaccinated with MCV4 (n=17) or MPSV4 (n=13) and sampled at days 0, 7, 30, 180 and 750 showed that both vaccines induced robust polysaccharide-specific IgG binding antibody responses against serogroups A and C, peaking at day 30 for MCV4 and day 180 for MPSV4, with greater magnitude and duration after MPSV4 than after a single dose of MCV4.

sources.quote: Both vaccines induced robust polysaccharide-specific IgG binding antibody responses against serogroups A and C, as measured by ELISA. These responses peaked at day 30 (MCV4) or day 180 (MPSV4) (Fig. 1a). The magnitude and duration of the polysaccharide-specific IgG response was greater with MPSV4 compared to a single dose of MCV4 (Fig. 1a).
In a > 2-year longitudinal study, we immunized 30 healthy young adults with either MCV4 (n=17) or MPSV4 (n=13)

comparison.finding: both vaccine groups showed robust polysaccharide-specific IgG binding antibody responses against serogroups A and C at day 0
both vaccine groups showed robust polysaccharide-specific IgG binding antibody responses against serogroups A and C at day 7
MCV4 responses peaked at day 30, while MPSV4 showed greater magnitude and duration than a single dose of MCV4 at day 30
MPSV4 responses peaked at day 180 and had greater magnitude and duration than MCV4 at day 180
MPSV4 maintained greater magnitude and duration of polysaccharide-specific IgG responses than MCV4 at day 750

claim_2.claim: Serum Bactericidal Assay analysis of serum from 30 healthy young adults vaccinated with MCV4 (n=17) or MPSV4 (n=13) and sampled at days 0, 7, 30, 180 and 750 showed that both vaccines induced a rapid increase in serum bactericidal activity by day 7, peaking at day 30, declining by day 180, and remaining substantially above baseline at day 750, with no difference between vaccine groups at two years.

sources.quote: Both vaccines induced a rapid increase in serum bactericidal activity (SBA), which was detectable as early as day 7, peaked at day 30, began to decline by day 180, yet remained substantially above baseline at day 750 (Fig. 1d).

An SBA titer of 1:8 or higher, a correlate of protective immunity22, was maintained in the majority of MPSV4 and MCV4 vaccinees two years after inoculation, with no difference observed between the two vaccine groups (Fig. 1d).

comparison.finding: no difference between MCV4 and MPSV4 vaccine groups at day 0
both vaccines induced a rapid increase in serum bactericidal activity by day 7
both vaccines reached peak serum bactericidal activity at day 30
serum bactericidal activity declined by day 180 in both vaccine groups

no difference between MCV4 and MPSV4 vaccine groups at day 750; serum bactericidal activity remained substantially above baseline and SBA titer of 1:8 or higher was maintained in the majority of vaccinees

claim_3.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of blood from vaccinated adults showed that antibody secreting cells peaked 7 days after vaccination (day 7) in both MCV4 and MPSV4 recipients, but the magnitude of the ASC response induced by MPSV4 was lower than that induced by MCV4.

sources.quote: The number of peripheral blood antibody secreting cells (ASCs) induced by vaccination was assessed. The ASCs showed a peak at day 7 in both vaccines (Fig. 1f).

Surprisingly, even though a greater polysaccharide-specific antibody response was induced by MPSV4 (Fig. 1a, d), the magnitude of the ASC response induced by MPSV4 was lower than that induced by MCV4 (Fig. 1f).

comparison.finding: the magnitude of the antibody secreting cell (ASC) response at day 7 was lower in MPSV4 recipients than in MCV4 recipients

claim_4.claim: ELISpot analysis of blood cells from a subset of MCV4 vaccinees at 7 days after vaccination (day 7) showed that the majority of IgG antibody secreting cells detected in blood were specific for diphtheria toxoid rather than polysaccharide.

sources.quote: Polysaccharide- and DT-specific ELISpots in a subset of MCV4 vaccinees revealed that the majority of IgG ASCs detected in the blood at day 7 were specific for DT (Supplementary Fig. 1a, b).

claim_5.claim: Luminex xMAP analysis of serum from MCV4 vaccinees sampled at days 0, 7 and 30 showed that MCV4 elicited a strong anti-diphtheria toxoid IgG response at days 7 and 30 compared to baseline (day 0), whereas MPSV4 did not.

sources.quote: MCV4, which contains the diphtheria toxoid (DT) protein as a conjugate, elicited a strong anti-DT IgG response at days 7 and 30, whereas MPSV4 containing polysaccharide alone did not (Fig. 1e).
Immune response to Diphtheria toxoid (DT) carrier protein was assessed at Days 0, 7 and 30 using anti- DT IgG capture microsphere assay.

comparison.finding: baseline anti-diphtheria toxoid IgG at day 0
MCV4 elicited a strong anti-diphtheria toxoid IgG response at day 7, whereas MPSV4 did not
MCV4 elicited a strong anti-diphtheria toxoid IgG response at day 30, whereas MPSV4 did not

claim_6.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMCs from MCV4 and MPSV4 vaccinees sampled at days 0, 3 and 7 showed that 1,150 differentially expressed genes were identified in MCV4 vaccinees at day 7 compared to baseline (day 0), and these genes bore the hallmark of antibody secreting cells.

sources.quote: To gain insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying the responses to meningococcal vaccines, we analyzed the transcriptomic profiles in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC, days 0, 3 and 7) of the vaccinees using DNA microarrays (Table 1). At day 7 post-vaccination, we identified 1,150 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in MCV4 vaccinees (Fig. 2a). These DEGs bear the hallmark of antibody secreting cells (ASC), which is consistent with the enhanced frequencies of these cells (Fig. 1f).

comparison.finding: at day 7, 1,150 differentially expressed genes were identified in MCV4 vaccinees, and these genes bore the hallmark of antibody secreting cells

claim_7.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMCs from MCV4 and MPSV4 vaccinees sampled at days 0, 3 and 7 showed that only a small number of differentially expressed genes were identified at day 3 after vaccination (day 3) for both MPSV4 and MCV4, and at day 7 after vaccination (day 7) for MPSV4, compared to baseline (day 0).

sources.quote: However, only a small number of DEGs were identified at day 3 post-vaccination for both MPSV4 and MCV4, and at day 7 for MPSV4 (Fig. 2a).

comparison.finding: baseline day 0 samples from MCV4 and MPSV4 vaccinees were profiled
only a small number of differentially expressed genes were identified at day 3 for both MCV4 and MPSV4
at day 7, only MPSV4 had a small number of differentially expressed genes identified

claim_8.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMCs across five vaccine datasets showed that several B cell genes, including TNFRSF17, were up-regulated 7 days after vaccination (day 7) in both MCV4 and TIV compared to baseline, whereas innate immunity and interferon response genes including OAS1, OAS2, STAT1, STAT2 and TRIM22 were up-regulated 3 days after vaccination (day 3) with live attenuated virus vaccines.

sources.quote: Several B cell genes were up-regulated at day 7 in MCV4 and TIV vaccines (Fig. 3b), including TNFRSF17, a B cell differentiation gene that is predictive of antibody responses to the YF-17D and TIV vaccines4, 6. Genes associated with innate immunity and interferon responses, such as OAS1, OAS2, STAT1, STAT2 and TRIM22 were up-regulated at day 3 post-vaccination with live attenuated virus vaccines (Fig. 3b).

claim_9.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of PBMCs showed that increased activity of the Plasma cells-Immunoglobulin blood transcription module at 7 days after MCV4 vaccination (day 7) correlated with later DT-specific IgG responses.

sources.quote: Indeed, the increased activity of this module at day 7 MCV4 data is well correlated to later DT-specific IgG response (Fig. 4e), and it is consistent with the increase of antibody secreting cells at day 7 (Fig. 1f).

claim_10.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of blood transcriptomes at 3 days after vaccination (day 3) showed three distinct antibody-correlation patterns: a protein recall response shared by TIV and MCV4 anti-DT, a polysaccharide response shared by MPSV4 and MCV4 anti-PS, and a primary viral response for YF-17D.

sources.quote: Yet to our surprise, the early BTM correlation profiles at day 3 displayed three distinctive patterns (Fig. 5a and Supplementary Fig. 11) that represent the protein recall response (shared by TIV and MCV4 anti-DT), the polysaccharide response (shared by MPSV4 and MCV4 anti-PS) and primary the viral response (YF-17D).

claim_11.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of blood transcriptomes in the primary viral response showed that higher antibody response was associated with greater activity in interferon response and cell adhesion modules, while several cell division modules including PLK1 signaling events were inversely correlated with antibody response.

sources.quote: In the primary viral response (Fig. 5a, b, Supplementary Fig. 12), higher antibody response is associated with greater activity in interferon response and cell adhesion modules.
Inversely correlated to the antibody response are a number of cell division modules, including PLK1 signaling events.

claim_12.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of blood transcriptomes at 3 days after vaccination (day 3) showed that the anti-polysaccharide response contained modules associated with antigen presenting cells, their activation, complement, and proinflammatory cytokines in MPSV4 and MCV4 anti-PS responses.

sources.quote: The anti-polysaccharide response at day 3 (Fig. 5a, top; Supplementary Fig. 12) contains a number of modules associated with antigen presenting cells and their activation, as well as complement and proinflammatory cytokines (Fig. 5b).

claim_13.claim: Flow Cytometry and ELISA analysis of human dendritic cells stimulated in vitro showed that MPSV4 induced maturation of blood myeloid dendritic cells with up-regulation of co-stimulatory molecules and secretion of IL-6, TNF and IL-12p40, whereas MCV4 did not induce robust activation of dendritic cells in vitro.

sources.quote: The polysaccharide vaccine MPSV4 was able to induce the maturation of blood myeloid DC isolated from human PBMC (Supplementary Fig. 15). Up-regulation of co-stimulatory molecules and secretion of IL-6, TNF and IL-12p40 was detected in human DCs stimulated by MPSV4 (Fig. 6a).

However, despite there being a correlation of the DC surface signature module to anti-polysaccharide IgG (Supplementary Figure 14b), MCV4 did not induce robust activation of DCs in vitro (Fig. 6a & Supplementary Fig. 16).

claim_14.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of mouse splenic CD11c+ dendritic cells showed that dendritic cell maturation induced by MPSV4 depended on Myd88, Trif and Tlr4, as well as inflammasome activation, compared to knockout conditions.

sources.quote: Using these cells from the appropriate knockout mice, we demonstrated that DC maturation induced by MPSV4 is dependent on Myd88, Trif and Tlr4, as well as inflammasome activation (Fig. 6b, Supplementary Fig. 16).

comparison.finding: MPSV4-induced dendritic cell maturation depended on Myd88 and was reduced under Myd88 knockout conditions
MPSV4-induced dendritic cell maturation depended on Trif and was reduced under Trif knockout conditions
MPSV4-induced dendritic cell maturation depended on Tlr4 and was reduced under Tlr4 knockout conditions
MPSV4-induced dendritic cell maturation depended on inflammasome activation and was reduced under inflammasome-deficient knockout conditions
